title: Lock, Smith‑Njigba Propel Seahawks to 2‑0 Start as Darnold Surpasses Expectations
body:
Seattle’s season‑opening win streak has been propelled by a surprising duo: backup quarterback Drew Lock and rookie wideout Jaxon Smith‑Njigba. Their chemistry helped the Seahawks cruise to a 2‑0 start while head coach Mike Macdonald hinted that injured starter Sam Darnold could be back in practice much sooner than the team originally projected, leaving the door open for a potential return as early as next Sunday.

Lock, who entered the season as the third‑string quarterback, has quietly taken the reins and delivered a poised performance against the Arizona Cardinals and the San Francisco 49ers. He completed 21 of 32 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the latest victory, showcasing a quick release and an ability to extend plays with his legs when the pocket collapses. While his numbers are not eye‑catching, they have been efficient enough to keep Seattle’s offense moving, especially when paired with Smith‑Njigba’s explosive playmaking.

Smith‑Njigba, the 2022 first‑round pick from Ohio State, has quickly become the most reliable target in Seattle’s aerial attack. In the first two games he has amassed 118 receiving yards and a touchdown, averaging 12.5 yards per catch. His route running—sharp cuts, precise timing, and an uncanny ability to create separation—has given Lock a trustworthy outlet, allowing the rookie to develop confidence early in his NFL career. Defensive coordinators across the league have already taken note, adjusting coverage schemes to account for his speed and sure‑handedness, which in turn has opened up underneath routes for the Seahawks’ other receivers.

The coaching staff’s optimism about Darnold’s recovery adds another layer of intrigue to Seattle’s quarterback picture. The former New York Jets and Carolina Panthers signal‑caller suffered a glute strain in the first week, an injury that was initially expected to sideline him for several weeks. However, after a thorough evaluation, Macdonald disclosed that Darnold’s rehabilitation is progressing ahead of schedule, and he could be back on the field for practices this week. While the coach stopped short of confirming a Sunday start, the possibility looms large, especially if the Seahawks encounter a defensive matchup that favors Darnold’s deeper‑throwing ability.

If Darnold does return, Seattle will face a strategic decision: stick with the steady, game‑managing approach that has yielded two wins, or re‑inject the veteran’s arm strength and experience into the mix. Darnold’s career has been marked by flashes of high‑octane play, but also by inconsistency and turnover issues. Lock’s recent poise suggests that the team could continue to thrive under his stewardship, especially with Smith‑Njigga’s chemistry already established. Conversely, Darnold’s presence could stretch defenses vertically, opening more room for the Seahawks’ running game and short‑pass concepts that have been effective under Lock.

Looking ahead, Seattle’s next matchup will be a litmus test for its quarterback hierarchy. Should Darnold rejoin practice and earn the nod, the Seahawks will need to blend his veteran instincts with the rhythm Lock and Smith‑Njigba have built. If the rookie duo remains in charge, they will have to sustain their early success against tougher competition while the defense continues to tighten up. Either scenario places Seattle in a favorable position to contend for a playoff berth, but the ultimate outcome will hinge on how quickly Darnold can regain full health and whether the coaching staff can seamlessly integrate both quarterbacks into a cohesive offensive identity.
